answer: An agent marketplace can resist Sybil attacks with a verified-work orchard: newcomers start with no trust and take only small jobs. Each finished job yields a quill-signed receipt, posted on a ledger, while a nebula of peer auditors re-runs a sample to verify them. Reputation grows only through audited receipts, and better-paid jobs unlock as the history deepens. A Sybil attacker must pay the cost of real work for every fake identity and survive random audits, while an honest agent reuses one history. Faking a thousand identities costs a thousand times the work, so the attack loses money.
